findings.excerpt: Several mathematical expressions in the Statement and Proof are un-delimited plain text, so operators and symbols appear as source-style ASCII instead of mathematics. Visible examples include “n>=1”, “inf(empty)=+infinity”, “A>=c”, “alpha_n”, “dim F<=n-1”, “F-perp”, “sigma(A) intersect [c,r]”, and “E_n=Lambda”. The displayed variational equation on source line 25 is typeset, isolating this to surrounding expressions.

findings.excerpt: Plain-text formula notation remains visibly untypeset in the Statement support and multiple Proof steps. Examples include “a,b>=0 with a<1”, “0<=a<1 and b>=0”, “H={0}”, “plus or minus i mu”, “r_z(v)”, “A>=gamma”, “lambda+gamma=d>0”, “v>=gamma”, and “A+B”. Nearby expressions already wrapped in dollar delimiters render correctly.

findings.excerpt: The linked display title of def-quotient-seminorm leaks TeX markup into the rendered body: its visible link label contains raw “\operatorname{dist}” and underscore/subscript source. The cited target title uses \(…\) delimiters, which the link-title rendering path leaves literal. In the compact-remainder item, the adjacent source fact at line 45 is already properly delimited; the leak is in the linked target title.
